abstract: BACKGROUND: Advanced seminoma is a rare clinicopathologic entity. To the authors' knowledge, very few sizeable reports published to date have studied the outcome of patients with advanced seminoma after first-line and salvage therapy, and few have dealt with prognostic factors initially or in patients with recurrent disease. METHODS: The records of 145 men with advanced seminoma who were treated with cisplatin-based first-line chemotherapy regimens were reviewed. Six patient characteristics, including age, prior radiotherapy, primary tumor site, initial serum lactate dehydrogenase and human chorionic gonadotropin levels, and disease stage, were studied as initial prognostic factors. In patients with recurrent disease, outcome according to the site of recurrence and the salvage treatment was also reviewed. RESULTS: A complete response was obtained in 130 patients (90%) after cisplatin-based first-line chemotherapy, and the 5-year overall survival rate was 81% (95% confidence interval [95% CI], 73-87%). Nonpulmonary visceral metastasis at diagnosis was the only initial adverse prognostic factor. Thirty-one patients (21%) developed recurrent disease. Recurrence in the liver or the central nervous system was a major adverse prognostic factor, with a 5-year overall survival rate of 7% (95% CI, 1-32%), compared with 58% (95% CI, 33-79%) in patients who had lymph node, lung, or bone recurrences. The only durable complete remission after a liver recurrence was obtained with high-dose chemotherapy followed by autologous stem cell transplantation. All 12 patients who were treated for primary mediastinal seminoma with cisplatin-based chemotherapy alone were long-term disease free survivors. CONCLUSIONS: Overall, the prognosis of patients with advanced seminoma was good after cisplatin-based, first-line chemotherapy. Metastasis in the liver or the central nervous system, initially or at recurrence, is currently the only proven adverse prognostic factor.
abstract_ja:
背景：進行セミノーマは稀な臨床病理学的疾患である。著者らの知る限り、進行セミノーマ患者の一次治療およびサルベージ治療後の転帰を検討した大規模な報告はごく少数であり、初診時の予後因子や再発例の予後因子を扱った報告もほとんどない。
方法：シスプラチン併用の一次化学療法レジメンを受けた進行セミノーマの男性145例の記録を後方視的に検討した。初期予後因子として、年齢、既往の放射線療法、原発部位、初診時の血清乳酸脱水素酵素およびヒト絨毛性ゴナドトロピン(hCG)値、病期分類の6つの患者特性を検討した。再発例では、再発部位およびサルベージ治療による転帰も検討した。
結果：シスプラチン併用の一次化学療法後、130例(90%)で完全奏効が得られ、5年全生存率は81%(95%信頼区間[95% CI]、73-87%)であった。初診時の肺以外の内臓転移が、唯一の初期の不良な予後因子であった。31例(21%)が再発した。肝または中枢神経系への再発は主要な不良予後因子であり、5年全生存率は7%(95% CI、1-32%)であった。これに対し、リンパ節、肺、骨への再発例では58%(95% CI、33-79%)であった。肝再発後に持続的な完全寛解が得られたのは、大量化学療法に続く自家幹細胞移植のみであった。縦隔原発セミノーマに対しシスプラチン併用化学療法のみで治療された12例は、全例が長期無病生存者であった。
結論：全体として、シスプラチン併用の一次化学療法後の進行セミノーマの予後は良好であった。初診時であれ再発時であれ、肝または中枢神経系への転移が、現時点で唯一証明された不良な予後因子である。
